source_text: 30 IUDICIBUS SIBI PLACENTIBUS. Intuite dicta Salominis, iudices omnes, Uno uerbo suo qualiter uos ille detractat: Dona quam et xenia corrumpunt iudices omnes! Inde 'nimis', sequit<ur>, 'datorem semper amatis', Cum quaerit<ur>, causa uictoriam tollit iniqua. Innocens hic ego sum, nec uos incuso pusillus, Blasphemium tollat Salomon, qui <clamat> aperte. 'Uobis autem Deus est uenter et praemia iura.' Suggerit hoc Paulus apostolus, non ego pulex. Si locus aut tempus fauet aut persona prouenit, Iudex esto tuus. Quod nunc extolleris inde? Blasphema<s>, indocilis: de cuius praestantia uiuis, In fragilitate tanta non respicis umquam. Per gradu<m> et lucra auidus fortunae praesumis, Lex tibi non ulla est, nec te in prosperitate dignos Auro licet cenes cum turba choraulica semper Cruciarium Dominum si non adorasti, peristi. Et locus et tempus et persona tibi donatur, Nunc si tamen credis; sin autem, pro eo timebis. Tempera te Christo et ceruicem illi depone: Isti honor remanet et tota fiducia rerum. Blanditur quando tibi tempus nunc, cautior esto, Ultima fatorum non prouidens, quae te oportet. Sine Christo nec uixisse te conpotis unquam.
pass_a_gloss: Iudices: Dona/xenia corrupt. Venter = deus. Without Cruciarium Dominum adorasti → peristi. Tempera te Christo; ceruicem illi.
pass_b_english: Consider Solomon’s sayings, all you judges — how with one word he pulls you down: gifts and presents corrupt all judges! Thence follows: you always love the giver; when a cause is sought, an unjust cause carries the victory. I here am innocent, nor do I, a little one, accuse you — let Solomon take up the open charge. “But your god is the belly, and rewards are laws.” Paul the apostle suggests this, not I a flea. If place or time favors or a person advances, be judge of yourself. Why are you lifted from that? You blaspheme, untaught: from whose bounty you live, in such frailty you never look back. By rank and greedy gain you presume on fortune; you have no law, nor do you count yourself worthy in prosperity — though you may dine in gold with a piping crowd always. If you have not adored the crucified Lord, you have perished. Place and time and person are given you — now if you believe; if not, you will fear for that. Temper yourself to Christ and lay the neck down to him: that honor remains and the whole trust of things. When time flatters you now, be more wary, not foreseeing the last of the fates that must meet you. Without Christ you never even manage to have lived.
